newsitem.title: USA: UPI to close many European, Middle East bureaus.
newsitem.headline: UPI to close many European, Middle East bureaus.

text.p: United Press International is closing many of its bureaus in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, laying off about half of the 75 employees in those regions, a spokesman said on Tuesday.
"Most of our European bureaus are going to be closed," said Tom Johnson, director of marketing and sales for the news service. "We are not sure precisely how many and at what location."
"At the same time we will continue to provide global news" through a stringer network, Johnson said.
He said the London bureau would remain open and an Arabic service would be maintained. U.S. operations will not be affected.
UPI has 23 bureaus in Europe, the Middle East and Africa now, Johnson said. Worldwide the news service has 1,100 employees, including 400 full-time staffers.

"This is part of a strategic plan that was developed back in the spring," Johnson said. "What we are provisioning is a network that is going to provide faster news. A lot of our clients are broadcast media."
The news service was bought by a group of Saudi Arabian investors in 1992 after it filed for protection under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code.
